name: scenario-dependency-analyzer.advisory-lockfile-refresh
purpose: Refresh one surface's lockfile per scenario for advisories whose fix the declared ranges already admit: preview, optionally apply, re-preview to prove convergence; one bounded row per scenario.

scenarios.description: Scenario names separated by spaces or semicolons (commas also work in a program call, but `library run` reads a comma in --input as the next input), 1..12 per run; batch a larger fleet across runs.

advisories.description: all (every advisory Security Health reports on each scenario's surface; the default) or GHSA or CVE ids separated by spaces or semicolons, 1..8. The exposed packages are updated in one resolution.

parents.description: npm packages that may move with the advisory's packages when a parent pins a vulnerable version (express pins body-parser ~1.20.3 in older locks). Used only for a scenario whose advisory-only update leaves a package exposed and which locks the parent; the parent moves within its own declared range.

surface.description: Surface whose lockfile is refreshed in every scenario.

lock_only.description: true publishes only the lockfile: node_modules is not relinked, nothing is downloaded and no package store is written, so the write is kilobytes and a running scenario is untouched until its next governed setup. false also relinks node_modules (store growth; held to the install-sized disk floor).

apply.description: false previews only; true publishes each lockfile update and re-previews it. Run the preview first.

assumptions: scenario-dependency-analyzer is running and Security Health has current vulnerability evidence for the scenarios (the advisory selector and the exposure judgment read it)

the advisories are ones whose fix lies inside the declared ranges (a pinning parent named in parents may move with them); an advisory that needs a major bump is reported per scenario as no_fix_in_range and changes nothing
a running scenario keeps serving: only the lockfile changes and nothing is restarted, so the next governed setup or restart picks the lock up
apply=true is the caller's decision after reading the preview of the same inputs
invariants: no manifest range, approval record or generated file is written; the only effect is the lockfile update the owner's deps update verb performs under its own store, disk admission and rollback, and with lock_only (the default) node_modules and the package store are not touched
scenarios are handled one at a time, in input order, with no retry; a refusal or failure is that scenario's row and the run continues
an applied update is reported refreshed only after a re-preview shows the lockfile current and no package named exposed by the analyzer
an unreachable owner stops the run as unavailable with the remaining scenarios not attempted
the envelope is printed exactly once, on every path, below the 4096-byte stdout bound

signals.rows: one [scenario, status, detail] per scenario; row status is refreshed, would_update, already_fixed, not_exposed, no_fix_in_range, partly_fixed, not_converged, blocked, apply_failed or error
signals.attention: scenarios whose status is not refreshed, would_update, already_fixed or not_exposed
signals.rows_compacted: true when quiet rows were collapsed or trimmed to fit the output bound

budget.async_reason: each scenario is a staged package-manager resolution (a preview, an apply and a re-preview), so a batch of up to 12 exceeds the 120 s synchronous bound

fixtures.note: Preview only: react-router's fix is outside the declared range, so the row is no_fix_in_range and nothing is published.
